scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'baseline_age' is listed among trial_measured_features so the feature is observed in the dataset. G2: TRUE — the hypothesis names concrete physiological steps (increased arterial stiffness, orthostatic susceptibility) that plausibly change tolerance to intensive BP lowering and raise rates of specific harms (syncope, AKI). G3: TRUE — the claim is a genuine treatment-effect modification mechanism (older/frail physiology increases treatment-related harms which can offset benefit), not solely an absolute-risk amplification. G4: TRUE — the interaction (reduced tolerability and altered risk–benefit in older/frail patients with intensive BP lowering) has support in clinical literature and subgroup analyses (e.g., concerns from RCTs and frailty-focused analyses showing different harm/benefit balances). G5: TRUE — the hypothesis proposes clear, operational subgroups (age bands and frailty strata) and gives explicit clinical recommendations, so it is actionable.
scored_features.justification: All gates passed; decisive was G3 because the hypothesis articulates a physiological mechanism (older/frail patients suffer more treatment-related harms) that makes this a true effect modifier rather than mere baseline-risk amplification.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'bmi' is present in trial_measured_features. G2: TRUE — the hypothesis specifies a concrete mechanism (obesity → volume-mediated hypertension → greater responsiveness to diuretics) linking BMI to differential pharmacologic blood-pressure lowering. G3: TRUE — this describes a plausible PD-mediated effect-modification (greater achievable SBP fall with diuretic regimens in obese patients) rather than only stating higher baseline risk. G4: FALSE — while physiological studies support obesity-related volume hypertension and diuretic responsiveness, there is limited direct RCT evidence showing a BMI × intensive-BP-target interaction on CV outcomes (and ACCORD medication classes were not randomized), so the specific feature×treatment outcome interaction is not clearly established in trial literature; G4 FALSE — cascade: G5 also FALSE. G5: FALSE — because G4 failed, actionable treatment rules based on BMI × regimen lack robust trial support.
scored_features.justification: Failed at G4: although a biologically coherent PD mechanism is proposed and G1–G3 pass, there is insufficient RCT-level literature demonstrating that BMI meaningfully modifies CV outcome benefit of intensive SBP targets via diuretic responsiveness, so clinical recommendations remain unsupported.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'sbp' is recorded in the trial_measured_features. G2: TRUE — the hypothesis names mechanistic considerations (achievable mmHg reductions, arterial stiffness limiting SBP fall) linking baseline SBP to treatment effects. G3: FALSE — the main argument is classic absolute-risk amplification (higher baseline SBP → larger absolute mmHg and absolute-event reductions) with no additional, well-specified pharmacodynamic mechanism that changes the relative treatment effect; G3 FALSE — cascade: G4 and G5 also FALSE. G4: FALSE — because G3 failed, the specific SBP×treatment interaction beyond baseline-risk arithmetic is not established. G5: FALSE — no new actionable subgroup beyond the obvious high-versus-low baseline SBP is justified by an HTE mechanism in this formulation.
scored_features.justification: Failed at G3: the hypothesis is principally an absolute-risk amplifier (higher baseline SBP → larger absolute benefit) rather than asserting a distinct pharmacologic/pathophysiologic change in how the intervention works, so it does not meet the HTE criterion.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'dbp' appears in the trial_measured_features. G2: TRUE — the hypothesis specifies a concrete physiologic pathway (low DBP reduces coronary perfusion pressure → increased myocardial ischemia risk when DBP is further lowered) consistent with a J-curve mechanism. G3: TRUE — this is a plausible effect modifier: low baseline DBP could make intensive SBP lowering cause increased ischemic harm (a treatment-mediated adverse effect), not merely reflect baseline prognosis. G4: TRUE — the DBP 'J-curve' and concern about low DBP in patients with CAD have support across observational studies and randomized-trial subgroup discussions (clinical literature has repeatedly raised and examined this interaction). G5: TRUE — the proposal gives clear DBP bands and CAD-stratified recommendations that are operationalizable in clinical practice.
scored_features.justification: All gates passed; decisive was G3 because the hypothesis advances a mechanistic treatment-modifying pathway (low DBP → impaired coronary perfusion → increased ischemic harm with intensive lowering) rather than only predicting absolute-risk differences.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'hr' is included in the trial_measured_features. G2: FALSE — the hypothesis mainly treats heart rate as a prognostic marker of sympathetic tone and baseline risk and does not specify a clear pharmacodynamic or pathophysiologic chain by which intensive BP lowering would act differently in high-HR patients (the proposal is conditional and conflated with confounders like beta-blocker use and arrhythmia). G2 FALSE — cascade: G3..G5 also FALSE.
scored_features.justification: Failed at G2: the hypothesis lacks a concrete mechanistic chain (it largely treats HR as a baseline risk marker confounded by medications/arrhythmia) so it does not meet the biological-coherence requirement for an HTE claim.
